risk_if_not_implemented: Without Incident Response Plan (IRP), security incidents may not be detected, contained, investigated or communicated in a timely manner, increasing their scope, duration and cost. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unperformed / Unowned Control Responsibilities (R-GV-3), Uncontrolled Internal Security / Privacy Exposure (R-GV-4), Inability to Demonstrate Due Diligence / Due Care (R-GV-9), Delayed Containment / Increased Incident Impact (R-IR-2), and most likely increases susceptibility to Human Error (MT-9).

compensating_control_1.name: Incident Response Training
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to train personnel in their incident response roles and responsibilities.
compensating_control_1.justification: Incident Response Training (IRO-10) provides personnel training and awareness that compensates for the absence of Incident Response Plan (IRP) (IRO-08) by reducing human-factor risk by equipping personnel to recognize and respond to relevant threats. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Business Continuity Management System (BCMS)
compensating_control_2.description:
Mechanisms exist to operate a Business Continuity Management System (BCMS) to achieve resilient Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) during:
(1) Routine operations; and
(2) Adverse conditions.
compensating_control_2.justification: Business Continuity Management System (BCMS) (BCD-02) provides resilience and recovery capability that compensates for the absence of Incident Response Plan (IRP) (IRO-08) by ensuring the organization can restore operations and data when the primary control is absent. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
